To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the substitution of Ru by a small amount of Ir in RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 9 (RSCO) results in the suppression of the ferromagnetic (FM) and superconducting (SC) transitions, but the SC state is still present in the Ir-doped RSCO samples up to x = 0.10, with the highest H c2 ( 0 ) value being 52 T.

Ir doping in Ru 1−x Ir x Sr 1− x Ce 0.5 Gd 0.5 Cu 2 O 10+δ ( x =0.05,0.075,0.10) suppresses both the ferromagnetic and superconducting transitions, however, the superconducting phase survives up to the highest magnetic field applied, and that the superconductivity in this system can be described by the JJA model.
the partial substitution of Ir for Ru in RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 6+ δ leads to a suppression of both the magnetic and superconductive properties, with no significant structural changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of Ir substitution in Ru 1−x Ir x Sr 1−y Eu y Gd 1+ y Cu 2 O 7+ y, where 0 ⪡  x  ≤ 0.10 and 0 ⫹  y  ⫹ x  ⫺ 1.
the effects of Ir doping on the physical properties of the ferromagnetic Ru-based cuprates.
the effects of the partial substitution of Ir for Ru on the magnetic and the electronic superconducting states of RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 7.5 + δ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Ir substitution in the ruthenocuprates suppresses the ferromagnetism and superconducting states, and the superconductivity is still present up to the highest Ir concentration of x  = 0.10, which is the highest doping level reported so far for the RuSr 2 Gd x Ce 1− x Cu 2 O 10−δ system.
the Ir-doping does not significantly alter the superconducting and magnetic properties of the rutheno-cuprates.
Ir doping suppresses the ferromagnetic order and the superconductivity in these materials, but the superconducting properties are not affected in a strong manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the partial substitution of the magnetic Ru ions by Ir ions, which are nonmagnetic, does not change significantly the superconducting properties in these ruthenates, but the magnetic properties are strongly affected.
the Ir substitution in the Ru 1− y Gd 1+ y Sr 2 Cu 2 O 7− δ system has the effect of decreasing the superconducting volume fraction and increasing the critical current density.
the Ir substitution in RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 6+ x ruthenocuprate leads to a suppression of the superconducting and magnetic states and a decrease in the transition width.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the superconductivity is preserved in these materials up to high Ir concentrations and that the Ir substitution is a good way to control the magnetic properties of this class of materials, which could be of great interest for the development of new devices.
Ir doping in the ferromagnet RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 7.9 is an effective way of suppressing the ferromagnetic order, and hence, the ferromagnetic-superconducting coupling.

the ruthenocuprates Ru 1−x Ir x Sr 1− x Gd x Cu 2 O 7−δ are a good example of a ferromagnetic superconducting system with a very weak interplay between the magnetic and superconductive orders, which is a key feature for a possible application of the ruthenocuprates in high temperature superconducting devices.
